drafts.title: Provide physical one‑touch controls for the most frequent functions
drafts.description: Customers can operate the most commonly used functions (volume, quick climate adjustments, and media playback) using dedicated tactile, one‑touch controls without looking at the central display.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In a usability test, participants must be able to complete the three target actions (volume up/down, temperature +/-2°C, play/pause) using the physical controls within 3 seconds and without glancing at the central display in at least 90% of attempts.
assumptions: Physical controls can be integrated into the cabin layout without causing ergonomics regressions.
Customers will prefer a mix of tactile and touchscreen controls for frequent tasks.
uncertainties: Exact number and placement of physical controls that balance aesthetics and usability.
Potential differences in preference across customer age groups.

drafts.title: Retain and optimize the large, curved information display as a selling point
drafts.description: Customers experience a large, easily readable curved display that improves perceived modernity and helps with overview of vehicle status and media/navigation.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: At least 80% of participants in a perception study rate the display's legibility and helpfulness as 4/5 or higher when completing common tasks (navigation glance, media selection, range check).
assumptions: Large-format displays continue to be perceived as a premium differentiator in 3–5 years.
uncertainties: How future UI styles or ambient lighting conditions affect perceived benefit.

drafts.title: Make remaining range trustworthy and transparent, especially in winter
drafts.description: Customers receive remaining range predictions they trust because the system explains uncertainty and matches real driving experience even under cold weather conditions.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In winter test cycles, the predicted remaining range must deviate by no more than 10% from measured real‑world range in at least 90% of test runs; the UI must surface an uncertainty range (±X km) or confidence level for every prediction.
assumptions: Improved algorithms and richer vehicle/sensor/temperature data will be available to the vehicle within 3–5 years.
Access to historic and live energy consumption patterns is feasible while respecting privacy rules.
uncertainties: Magnitude of improvement achievable from prediction models vs. hardware limitations (battery thermal behavior).
Variability of accuracy across extreme climates and driver behaviors.

drafts.title: Help customers find and evaluate public chargers (availability and condition) from the car
drafts.description: When planning a trip or searching nearby, customers see charger locations plus current availability status and basic condition information so they can choose reliable chargers with confidence.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: For searches within the primary market, the system must display availability/status and at least one condition attribute (e.g., working/unknown/out of service) for at least 90% of publicly listed chargers; for route planning, recommended chargers lead to successful charging sessions in at least 85% of tested routes.
assumptions: Data sharing between operators and vehicle platforms will improve and roaming/aggregation services will be available.
Real‑time or near‑real‑time status feeds will be accessible for a significant portion of chargers.
uncertainties: Coverage and quality of third‑party charging data vary by region and operator.
Legal or commercial restrictions could limit availability of station status data.

drafts.title: Provide a usable front storage compartment (frunk) with meaningful capacity
drafts.description: Customers have a dedicated front storage area that noticeably increases usable luggage space compared with the current cabin, allowing easy carriage of everyday items.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: A dedicated front storage compartment with at least 70 liters of usable volume and the ability to stow two standard carry‑on sized bags (measured in a standard packing test) must be available in at least one successor configuration.
assumptions: Vehicle architecture and packaging choices will allow reconfiguration of front space without impairing crash, HVAC, or other systems.
Customers value additional front storage even if it affects some other trunk/layout tradeoffs.
uncertainties: Exact usable volume achievable given packaging constraints (electric components, HVAC).
Impact on front passenger ergonomics and HVAC performance.

drafts.title: Ensure hands‑free tailgate gesture is reliable and predictable
drafts.description: Customers using the foot gesture to open the trunk experience reliable opening when intended and minimal accidental openings.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: The hands‑free tailgate opens in response to a defined foot gesture within 0.5 m in at least 95% of valid gestures during trials, and false positive openings occur in less than 2% of parking events.
assumptions: Improved sensor algorithms and calibration can reduce false positives and increase sensitivity.
Physical placement and ground clearance of the rear bumper will support a reliable detection zone.
uncertainties: Performance variance across footwear types, luggage handling, and snow/mud conditions.
Potential need for user education or adaptive sensitivity settings.

drafts.title: Keep and protect the high level of ride comfort customers value today
drafts.description: Customers experience the same or better ride comfort on real roads, retaining the current car’s comfortable behavior across typical urban, highway and rough road scenarios.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In controlled route comparisons, at least 90% of participants must rate the successor’s ride comfort as equal or better than the current baseline (score ≥4/5) across urban, highway and poor‑surface segments.
assumptions: Chassis and suspension choices for successor vehicles will allow maintaining or improving current comfort characteristics.
Customer perception tests remain a valid measure of comfort across model generations.
uncertainties: Trade‑offs between comfort and sportiness for different market variants.
Impact of increased vehicle weight (electrification) on perceived comfort.

drafts.title: Provide robust degraded/offline charging and navigation fallback
drafts.description: When live charger status or connectivity is unavailable, customers still receive useful charger suggestions and range estimates so they can continue a trip with minimal disruption.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: If live charging data are unavailable, the system must still present plausible charger locations within 5 km of the vehicle’s planned route and provide an estimated energy impact that deviates less than 15% from actual consumption in 90% of tested degraded scenarios.
assumptions: Local map and historical charger datasets can be stored and updated periodically on the vehicle.
On‑board models can produce usable estimates without live operator feeds.
uncertainties: Performance limits in regions with sparse charger infrastructure or frequently changing station availability.
How long cached data remains valid without connectivity.
